name: Splendor

key_numbers.label: Prestige points that trigger the end
Token limit at end of turn

setup.text: Shuffle the three development decks separately and stack them in a column, level 1 at the bottom to level 3 at the top.
Shuffle the noble tiles and reveal one more than the number of players. Return the rest to the box.
Sort the gem tokens by colour into 6 piles within reach of everyone. Leave the gold alone.

by_count.2: Take 3 tokens of each gem colour out of the game, leaving 4 of each.
by_count.3: Take 2 tokens of each gem colour out of the game, leaving 5 of each.
by_count.4: Use all 7 tokens of each gem colour.

setup.text: The youngest player goes first; play passes clockwise.

turn.summary: Do exactly one of four actions, then check whether a noble visits you.
steps: Take 3 gem tokens of three different colours.
Or take 2 gem tokens of the same colour, but only if at least 4 of that colour are in the pile.
Or reserve 1 card and take 1 gold token. Take the card from the face-up display or blind from the top of a deck.
Or buy 1 card, either face up in the middle or one you reserved on an earlier turn.
Refill any gap in the display at once from the same level's deck.
End your turn with no more than 10 tokens, gold included. Return extras, including ones you just took.
Check the nobles: if you hold enough bonuses for one, take its tile. You get at most one per turn.

end: When a player reaches 15 prestige points, finish the round so that everyone has had the same number of turns. The player with the most prestige points then wins.

scoring.text: Each development card shows its prestige points, if any.
Each noble tile you have is worth 3 prestige points.
Count your nobles in the final total.

tiebreak: The tied player who bought the fewest development cards wins.

missed.text: Each card you own gives a bonus of its colour that counts as a token of that colour when paying. Enough bonuses can make a card free.
A gold token replaces any colour when buying a card.
Taking 2 tokens of one colour needs at least 4 of that colour in the pile before you take them.
With no gold left you can still reserve a card; you just get no gold.
A noble visit is automatic, cannot be refused and is not an action. Only bonuses count towards it, not tokens. If several nobles qualify, choose one.
Reserved cards stay in hand and can only be bought by you. You cannot discard them.

not_covered: Solo play is not in this rulebook.
